title: Claude's answering style

body.text: Claude automatically adapts its style to the context. For technical questions it answers in detail and with structure; for casual chat it keeps things short and friendly.
Claude doesn't always answer in black and white
— especially for complex questions, it tends to lay out both sides and give a
more nuanced, deeper perspective than a typical answer
so you can decide with full information.

example: "What are the pros and cons of using AI at work? Give me a well-rounded view."

title: You can customize the answering style

body.text: You can tell Claude directly how you want it to answer — short, casual, or expert. Claude can also
mimic a tone and writing style
from an example you give it.
Assigning Claude a role or persona
— like "answer as a financial advisor" or "answer like a teacher for kids" — helps you get a response that fits exactly what you need.

example: "Answer like a close friend who's an investing expert: how should I start saving if I have 3,000 baht left over each month?"

question: If you want Claude to answer short and concise, what should you do?

options.text: You can't adjust it — Claude always answers the same way
Tell Claude directly in your prompt that you want a short answer
You have to switch the model first

question: When you ask Claude a complex question, how does it tend to answer?

options.text: It refuses to answer complex questions
It gives multiple perspectives and a deeper answer

question: What's the benefit of giving Claude a persona like 'answer as a financial advisor'?

options.text: It gets you an answer better matched to the context and your needs
It gives Claude real-time data access

question: Claude's answer is too long and you want it concise. What should you do?

options.text: Say clearly: "answer short and concise, as bullets, no more than 5 points"

question: Setting a persona like "answer as a financial advisor" helps with what?

options.text: Tuning the perspective and expertise level to fit the task
